name: Posture Recovery from Carni
description: Against Carni, release the shoulder clamp, triceps control and head-side leg before raising posture. The trapped limb is the arm, not the lower leg.
summary: Posture recovery against Carni must free the shoulder clamp, triceps control and head-side leg before the top player raises the chest.
overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Carni; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. Carni attacks the shoulder. A Saddle counter or lower-leg extraction is not implied by the configuration.

A leg clearing the head with an overhook is an upper-body trap, even if a butterfly hook remains below. Avoid reaching away while the opponent sets the triceps control. Keep a balanced base and early inside frames; tap instead of moving against a completed choke or joint lock.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Richie Martinez — Carni shoulder lock from Z guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iClQ2Np-n30).

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Carni (top): Which structure must be freed before you lift the chest?
flashcards.answer: Carni threatens the shoulder; free the triceps and head-side leg connection before raising posture.

plausible: Only wrist below retained triceps
Only head above the high knee

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Carni (top): Where should the elbow stay before triceps control closes?
flashcards.answer: Keep the elbow compact early rather than reaching into the developing shoulder clamp.
flashcards.answer_line: Elbow close to ribs without reaching

plausible: Straight across their torso
Behind your back as you turn out
trap: Long post above the opponent's head

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Carni (top): What forms an inside barrier before the shoulder clamp closes?
flashcards.answer: Use early inside frames while the shoulder can still move; a completed shoulder lock requires release.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside frames with a balanced base

plausible: Chest lift against the head-side leg
Wide post with upper arm outside
trap: Wrist grip with forearm outside gap

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Carni (top): How do you move while creating slack around the clamp?
flashcards.answer: Keep the head and captured arm aligned while opening space at the hip and thigh, rather than twisting through the clamp.
flashcards.answer_line: Keep the head and upper arm aligned

plausible: Head turned away with elbow pinned
Pull the wrist behind your hip

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Carni (top): When should the elbow withdraw from the high leg?
flashcards.answer: Free the upper-body connection before withdrawing the shoulder and elbow together.
flashcards.answer_line: After leg and triceps grips open

plausible: While only the wrist can move
Once a lower butterfly hook loosens
trap: When head rises despite the arm trap

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Carni (top): What confirms successful posture recovery?
flashcards.answer: Posture recovery requires actual shoulder release, not merely getting the head higher.

plausible: Head upright but elbow still pinned
Head-side leg down; triceps held
trap: Wrist free but upper arm clamped

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Carni (top): What does the head-clearing leg plus overhook indicate?
flashcards.answer: Recognize the overhook and head-side leg as shoulder-control geometry even if a butterfly hook remains below.

plausible: Posture clinch with upper arm free
Wrist grip with elbow unrestrained

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Carni (top): Why can lifting before arm release worsen the position?
flashcards.answer: Lifting against the retained upper arm can increase shoulder rotation; clear that connection first.

plausible: Head rise frees the triceps first
Trapped elbow follows chest freely
trap: Low hook loads; shoulder stays free

defender.name: Posture Recovery from Carni Defender
defender.description: Posture Recovery from Carni (defender): Use the guard and shoulder connection to bring the opponent close before moving the high leg. Manage the shoulder and neck line with a forearm frame as the leg clears the head.
defender.overview:
The top player faces a bottom guard player using Carni; the head, shoulder or arm may still be enclosed. Carni attacks the shoulder. A Saddle counter or lower-leg extraction is not implied by the configuration.

Use the guard and shoulder connection to bring the opponent close before moving the high leg. Manage the shoulder and neck line with a forearm frame as the leg clears the head. Turn partly belly down with the knee close and foot supported rather than wrenching the leg across the head.

Keep the captured arm connected so the opponent cannot freely roll or withdraw the shoulder. Hold the wrist and elbow at a comfortable angle; a small change can load the shoulder rapidly. Release the wrist and leg clamp immediately on a tap or when the partner needs to roll safely.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

As the shoulder clamp opens, rebuild guard retention with a frame on the side of the neck and hip movement that returns the knee shield. Keep the forearm inside against a crossface or chest pressure rather than following the freed arm with both hands.
key_principles: Set the upper-body angle: Use the guard and shoulder connection to bring the opponent close before moving the high leg.
Frame before clearing: Manage the shoulder and neck line with a forearm frame as the leg clears the head.
Anchor through the hips: Turn partly belly down with the knee close and foot supported rather than wrenching the leg across the head.
Hold the triceps: Keep the captured arm connected so the opponent cannot freely roll or withdraw the shoulder.
Control before finishing: Hold the wrist and elbow at a comfortable angle; a small change can load the shoulder rapidly.
Let the lock go: Release the wrist and leg clamp immediately on a tap or when the partner needs to roll safely.

flashcards.question: Posture Recovery from Carni (bottom): Which anchor helps keep the shoulder from rising?

plausible: Chase free wrist with arms extended
Keep turning with wrist still fixed
trap: Leave knees outside as chest settles
